title: A fake 'Jell-O diet' has fooled at least one celebrity: Could you be next?
description: Paris Hilton's mother, Kathy Hilton, recently tried the "Jell-O diet" to lose weight. She believed other celebrities—Oprah Winfrey, Doctor Oz, Michelle Obama and Kelly Clarkson—had endorsed it. But the diet was fake, and so were the endorsements. Both had been generated by artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Researchers find New Jerseyans want regulations around AI and mental health
description: Nearly 6 in 10 New Jersey adults support regulating how artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots interact with users seeking mental health advice, according to a study conducted by the Eagleton Center for Public Interest Polling, home of the Rutgers-Eagleton Poll, in collaboration with the Center for Health Services Research at the Rutgers Institute for Health, Health Care Policy and Aging Research.

title: Six in ten Indian companies believe AI to play a significant role: PWC
description: Indian manufacturers anticipate artificial intelligence significantly aiding strategic goals within five years. This optimism surpasses global counterparts regarding productivity and long-term growth potential. Automation adoption is led by data capture and analytics, followed by quality assurance. However, India lags in developing homegrown manufacturing capabilities and faces an MSME technology gap. Coherent integration of manufacturing capabilities will distinguish the Indian economy's future.

title: Is AI causing disruption in IT sector? L&TTS CEO Amit Chadha explains
description: L&T Technology Services CEO Amit Chadha explains how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an opportunity, not a threat, to the IT sector, driving expansion in engineering scope and demand for integrated capabilities. While AI boosts productivity, it fuels further demand for engineering talent due to accelerated development cycles and increased product complexity. The workforce is evolving to emphasize multi-disciplinary skills and deeper expertise, creating a capability-driven model.
